title: When the Homecoming Falls
premise: Juniper Vasquez, the statistician who keeps score from the safety of the bleachers, is paired with her nemesis—star athlete Theo Brandt—for a semester project documenting the team's season. As they dig into the numbers, Juniper uncovers evidence that the championship run is rigged by a booster club buying players' eligibility, and that Theo's scholarship depends on staying silent. Their uneasy alliance becomes real when exposing the truth threatens everything each of them has built their survival on. In the end, they forfeit the rigged title but win the game that matters: Juniper testifies before the school board, Theo walks away from the corrupt scholarship, and both finally claim a belonging they chose rather than inherited.
about_author: P. M. Joubert grew up in small-town Texas where Friday night lights outshone everything except the kids the town preferred not to see. A former high school debate coach, Joubert writes stories about outsiders who learn that belonging is something you build, not something you're granted.

chapters.title: The Counting Season
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Opening day of senior year; she catalogs classmates like data points and counts days to graduation, revealing her strategy of invisibility after years as the scholarship kid nobody claimed. When Coach Delgado announces a semester-long 'document the season' project with assigned partners, Juniper draws Theo Brandt—the boy who humiliated her freshman year. Beat: dread sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Nemesis Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. First forced collaboration in the empty gym: Theo wants to film highlight reels; Juniper wants statistical rigor. Their friction cracks open old wounds—she learns his arrogance masks a father who measures love in playing time. They strike a cold truce: minimal contact, maximum grade. Beat: grudging respect flickering under hostility.

chapters.title: Numbers Don't Cheer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Mid-season stats reveal impossible patterns: benchwarmers starting after booster meetings, penalty flags vanishing from game logs. She cross-references attendance sheets with donation records and finds a thread. When she shows Theo, he shuts down hard—his full-ride depends on this season staying clean. Beat: the first secret between them, heavier than rivalry.

chapters.title: What Theo Carries
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Homecoming week pressure mounts; his father and boosters host a dinner where Theo hears them discuss 'handling' an ineligible transfer player. He recognizes the machinery Juniper found—and realizes he was recruited into it. He almost tells Juniper, then watches her get publicly snubbed at the pep rally and can't bear adding to it. Beat: guilt crystallizing into complicity.

chapters.title: The Bleachers Burn
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Someone ransacks her project files and steals her stat notebook; only three people knew where she kept it. Suspecting Theo, she confronts him in the rain outside the field house, and instead of denial he hands her a copy of the booster club's eligibility ledger he photographed weeks ago. Beat: betrayal suspected, alliance truly forged.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Deal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair traces the ledger to athletic director Marsh, who offers Juniper a college recommendation and Theo a guaranteed pro-scout showcase in exchange for silence. Both are tempted—this is everything they've survived for. That night, working late, they admit why invisibility kept them safe, and something shifts between them beyond partnership. Beat: temptation at its sweetest, choice looming.

chapters.title: Falling
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marsh, sensing defection, leaks Juniper's scholarship status to the school paper, painting her as a disgruntled liar, and benches Theo with a fabricated injury report. Theo's father sides with the program. Stripped of the identities they performed, Juniper and Theo meet in the library and decide: finish the project as testimony. Beat: rock bottom becoming bedrock.

chapters.title: The Last Game That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Championship night against crosstown rivals. Knowing the outcome is bought, the team plays anyway—and Juniper, watching from the scorer's table, sees teammates play purely for each other. Theo, cleared to play one final quarter, gives everything despite the fix. They lose by two. It doesn't matter. Beat: grief transmuted into clarity about what winning means.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. At the school board hearing, Juniper presents the statistics and ledger while Theo testifies against his own recruitment, sacrificing the scholarship publicly. Marsh resigns mid-hearing; the state association launches an investigation. Theo's father walks out—but Theo doesn't follow. Outside, Juniper takes his hand, first time without pretense. Beat: the price paid, freely chosen.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue tone. Spring: the project wins state recognition, but the real inheritance is quieter—Juniper stops counting days because she's no longer serving a sentence. Theo enrolls at a smaller school on merit alone; they plant a memorial bench for the transfer player the system broke. Final line mirrors the opening count: zero days left, and she stays anyway. Beat: belonging earned, survival redefined.
